articles.body:
NBA training camps have officially begun!

Monday marked the arrival of media day for most of the league's 30 teams, with on-court practice beginning Tuesday -- exactly three weeks before the New York Knicks will raise their 2026 NBA championship banner.

We have you covered as you dig into the 2026-27 season, with roster breakdowns for all 30 teams, top storylines, decisions and lingering issues to watch over the next few weeks.

What to watch during training camp: the frontcourt

Despite the franchise's run to the Eastern Conference's No. 6 seed, Atlanta's lack of frontcourt size was a major weakness. The Hawks' defense ranked 18th in blocks and 29th in both second-chance and point paints allowed during the regular season. And in the playoffs, Atlanta trailed only the Denver Nuggets in second chance points allowed per game. Selecting forward Zuby Ejiofor at No. 23 in June's draft and re-signing center Jock Landale, who missed the Hawks' first-round defeat because of a right ankle sprain, will help. Mouhamed Gueye (fractured foot; might miss the start of 2026-27) and Henri Veesaar (torn right ACL; expected to miss the season).

What to watch during training camp: the offense

Over the past four regular seasons, Boston has won 73% of its games while also ranking in the top four leaguewide in 3-point attempts. But the Celtics' first-round loss to the Philadelphia 76ers revealed cracks in the NBA's second-ranked offense.

"The biggest thing is can we generate looks at the rim?" Celtics president of basketball operations Brad Stevens said. "Everybody wants to do that, and every one of us would prefer a dunk over a 3. Every single one of us. Those are hard to get, and we struggle to generate them."

With Jaylen Brown replaced by Paul George and Mitchell Robinson signed to provide frontcourt help, will the Celtics adjust their philosophy? Per Cleaning the Glass, George ranked in the 90th percentile among wings in midrange attempts. For his part, George also shot better than 39% on 3s for the ninth time in his career last season.

articles.headline: FA charges Fulham boss Álvaro Arbeloa with misconduct for comments after Man United draw
articles.description: Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa has been charged with misconduct by the FA  for claiming officials would "not let Manchester United lose" after Michael Carrick's side scored a late equaliser to draw their Premier League match at Craven Cottage.
articles.body:
Fulham boss Álvaro Arbeloa has been charged with misconduct by the Football Association for claiming officials would "not let Manchester United lose" after Michael Carrick's side scored a late equaliser to draw their Premier League match at Craven Cottage.

United were fortunate to leave with a point after Matheus Cunha's 89th-minute deflected goal snatched a 1-1 draw on Sept. 20.

In a post-match TV interview, Arbeloa said the referee had given "all fouls" for United and that "I knew after the game against Man City that they [would not] let Manchester United lose here," referencing the controversial VAR call in the Manchester derby.

The FA's misconduct charge alleges the Fulham manager "acted in an improper manner by making comments in a postmatch interview that imply bias and/or question the integrity of a match official."

Arbeloa -- who took over at Fulham in the summer but has yet to win a league game -- has until Thursday to provide a response.

- Patrick Dorgu returns to Man United after suspected hamstring injury with Denmark

- Chelsea charged by FA over alleged discriminatory chanting

United, meanwhile, have won just one game in their first five Premier League matches -- against Ipswich Town. They lost to Hull on the opening weekend, drew with Everton, lost to Man City and salvaged a draw against Fulham.

articles.headline: Sources: Packers, guard Kevin Zeitler agree to one-year deal
articles.description: Veteran guard Kevin Zeitler is signing a one-year deal with the Packers, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Another day, another former first-round draft pick signing for the Packers on the offensive line. The latest is Kevin Zeitler, a veteran guard who is signing a one-year deal with Green Bay on Wednesday, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Zeitler, 36, was the No. 27 pick in the 2012 NFL draft by the Cincinnati Bengals and has appeared in 214 games in his career. He is a native of Wisconsin, having grown up in the Milwaukee area and playing collegiately at the University of Wisconsin.

This comes after the Packers signed guard Laken Tomlinson (No. 28 pick in 2015) off the Dallas Cowboys practice squad Saturday and added Mekhi Becton (No. 11 pick in 2020) to their practice squad.

How the Packers (1-2) use the trio remains to be seen, but after their early-season struggles, they have undergone an in-season revamping at a position like never seen before under general manager Brian Gutekunst.

Green Bay ranks last in the NFL in rushing yards per game (48.7), and its 146 total rushing yards is the team's lowest through three games in a season since at least 1933. The Packers' 16% pass block win rate is the worst through the first three games of a season since ESPN began tracking it in 2017.

Zeitler has played most of his career at right guard, where first-year Packers starter Jacob Monk has struggled. Tomlinson has played mostly at left guard, where the Packers have started three different players in as many games. Becton has played on both sides and at both guard and tackle. The Packers lost right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele to a season-ending knee injury in the season opener.

When asked Tuesday whether the new linemen -- not including Zeitler, who had yet to sign -- could play this week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Packers offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich did not rule it out.

"Yeah, I think anything's a possibility, for sure, so we're going to do whatever we can to put the best guys out there," said Stenavich, who coached Tomlinson with the 49ers earlier in his career. "We've got to see where they're at and just where they're at with the playbook and the calls and everything like that, with the game plan. But yeah, everything's a possibility, and we're going to try and explore all avenues."

Zeitler played last season for the Tennessee Titans, for whom he promptly took over as their starting right guard. Entering the 2025 season, Titans general manager Mike Borgonzi described Zeitler as "one of the best guards in football."

He was a steadying presence next to JC Latham, who switched to right tackle from the left side in only his second NFL season. Zeitler started 16 games last season and played 864 (92%) of the Titans' offensive snaps.

Zeitler suffered a quadriceps injury during the Titans' Week 18 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. He also dealt with groin and biceps injuries that cut into his playing time in 2025.

articles.headline: Ex-NFL star Antonio Brown's hearing for expected plea deal postponed
articles.description: Former NFL star wide receiver Antonio Brown's court hearing where he was expected to accept a plea deal allowing him to avoid prison time in an attempted murder case was postponed Wednesday.
articles.body:
MIAMI -- Former NFL star wide receiver Antonio Brown's court hearing where he was expected to accept a plea deal allowing him to avoid prison time in an attempted murder case was postponed Wednesday.

Brown arrived in a Miami courtroom Wednesday morning and was ready to plead no contest to aggravated assault and be sentenced to probation, his lawyer said. But a Florida judge said she was in the middle of another trial and not ready to go forward with the plea deal. The hearing was pushed back to Oct. 28.

Brown is accused of grabbing a handgun from a security staffer after a celebrity boxing match in Miami on May 16, 2025, and firing two shots at a man he had been in a fistfight with earlier, according to an arrest warrant. Zul-Qarnain Kwame Nantambu told investigators one of the bullets grazed his neck.

Defense attorney Mark Eiglarsh said Brown was looking forward to putting the case behind him. Eiglarsh said the plea deal reached with prosecutors was too good to turn down and that it says Brown would not be considered a convicted felon.

"It's a setback because it's another month that my client has an ankle monitor on and doesn't have closure, which everybody in this care wants," Eiglarsh said after the hearing was postponed. He said he was "cautiously optimistic" the judge would agree to the terms.

Brown could face up to 30 years in prison if convicted of the original attempted murder charge. He has said on social media that he was defending himself from an attack and others were trying to steal jewelry from him.

Florida's Stand Your Ground law allows people who believe they face death or serious injury to use deadly force to defend themselves without a duty to retreat.

Richard Cooper, an attorney for Nantambu, has called the plea deal a fair one. He has said Nantambu forgives Brown and would not cooperate with law enforcement.

Brown, 38, spent 12 years in the NFL and was an All-Pro wide receiver who last played in 2021 for Tampa Bay, including winning a Super Bowl with quarterback Tom Brady.

Over the course of his career, much of it spent with Pittsburgh, he had 928 receptions for more than 12,000 yards and accounted for 88 total touchdowns, including punt returns and one pass.

During a 2021 game with Tampa Bay against the New York Jets, Brown took off his jersey, shoulder pads and gloves and ran off the field, leading to his release by the Buccaneers and effectively ending his career.

Brown has dealt with several legal problems over the years. He previously was accused of battery of a moving truck driver, several domestic violence charges, failure to pay child support and other incidents.

Brown was extradited in November 2025 from Dubai, where he has business interests, after an arrest warrant on the attempted murder charge was issued in June of the same year.

articles.headline: Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained
articles.description: The sporting world is waiting for a resolution to the hearings on Man City's charges for allegedly breaching the Premier League's financial rules. Here's what we know, and what might come next.
articles.body:
Editor's Note: This was originally published March 19, 2025. We have republished and updated this explainer of the facts -- the charges levied against Manchester City and the potential punishments -- along with insight as to the duration of the proceedings in light of Friday's news reports, which City are denying at this time. On Tuesday, Man City were found guilty of 100-plus charges related to these offenses, per a Premier League statement. Man City still deny all charges and have until Friday to appeal.

What are the charges against Manchester City?

They relate to the seasons between 2009-10 and 2022-23 and cover a range of alleged breaches -- the most serious being false accounting, with respect to providing accurate financial information on revenue (including sponsorship revenue), related parties and operating costs. There are other alleged breaches, including irregularities in player and manager remuneration and, in more recent seasons, failure to cooperate with the Premier League's investigation.

If the charges relate to alleged breaches, why are they coming to light only now?

Because much of this issue relates to the "Football Leaks," when internal documents -- "leaked" say the perpetrators, "stolen or false" say some of the victims -- relating to a range of soccer-related issues were made public. German newsmagazine Der Spiegel had access to the cache of documents -- including internal emails -- and published stories accusing Manchester City of flouting financial fair play rules, which regulate how clubs can generate revenue. This led to investigations by UEFA and, later, by the Premier League.

In February 2020, UEFA's investigation found Manchester City guilty and banned them from European football for two seasons while fining them €30 million. The ban was overturned five months later by the Court of Arbitration for Sport on the basis that some charges had exceeded the statute of limitations and others were "not established" by UEFA. City were also fined €10 million for failing to cooperate with the investigation.

Why is the Premier League's case taking so long?

It's a combination of the league's own rules and the many legal challenges City have brought over the years, contesting jurisdiction and other legal matters. Consider that officials only announced the investigation in March 2019, then went years without telling anyone what was going on or even if the case was dropped. (In fact, it was Her Majesty's Court of Appeals that informed us in 2021 that it was still ongoing, following another legal challenge.)

By the time the charges were brought, in February 2023, nearly 4½ years had passed. And the hearing itself didn't begin until Sept. 16, 2024, some 19 months later. That hearing lasted 12 weeks, until Dec. 6 of last year. articles.headline: Does Man City's guilty verdict impact Pep Guardiola's legacy as an all-time coaching great?
articles.description: Pep Guardiola won 16 major honors as Man City manager. They all now count for nothing after the Premier League found the club guilty of systematically breaking financial rules.
articles.headlineJa: マンCの有罪判決は、史上最高の名将ペップ・グアルディオラのレガシーに影響を与えるのか？
articles.descriptionJa: ペップ・グアルディオラ監督はマンCで16の主要タイトルを獲得した。しかし、プレミアリーグが同クラブによる組織的な財務ルール違反を認定したため、それらはすべて無意味なものとなってしまった。
articles.body:
Pep Guardiola won 16 major honors during his 10-year reign as Manchester City manager before he left in the summer. They all now count for nothing.

Under Guardiola, City won a Champions League-Premier League-FA Cup treble. They became the only club in English history to win four successive league titles. They were the first team to achieve a domestic treble, and the only side to win the title by amassing 100 points. All of it was built on a false premise.

To borrow a phrase from the Premier League statement that condemned the club's "systematic rule-breaking for almost a decade" following an independent commission's finding that City were guilty of more than 100 breaches of rules between 2009-2018, it was all a "sham."

- Marcotti: Hard to see how City recover from extraordinary guilty verdict

- Dawson: Man City's guilt the talk of the town around English soccer

- Watch: Full reaction to 'the biggest sporting cheating scandal ever'

The egregious actions of City's owners -- Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al Nahyan's Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) -- and executives has destroyed the reputation of a 146-year-old club. City have said they will appeal the verdict, and they maintain they are innocent, but Guardiola cannot escape the damage caused by a prolonged and systematic program of financial deception because much of it was done for his benefit.

Abu Dhabi built a club and a team fit for Guardiola, but it was a construction built by ill-gotten gains. The advantages Guardiola had at his disposal are now proved to have been unfair. As former Manchester United captain Roy Keane said this week: "[City] won it on the pitch because cheating was going on."

Financial mismanagement, chicanery, deception -- whatever you want to call it, the foundations of Guardiola's City empire are rooted in the rule-breaking that happened before and during his time as manager, so his record-breaking era at the club is tainted by all of it.

But there are two sides to the Guardiola story at City. The former Barcelona and Bayern Munich coach arrived at the Etihad in the summer of 2016 having already won six league titles in Catalonia and Bavaria, as well as two Champions Leagues with Barça. His status as the world's preeminent coach was already secure.

Guardiola is a coaching genius, a man whose tactical brilliance built arguably the world's greatest-ever club side at Barcelona. He reinvented the way the game was played, and his influence is now seen at every level of the game.

It's why City's Abu Dhabi hierarchy, led by Sheikh Mansour and club chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak -- who is also CEO of Mubadala, Abu Dhabi's sovereign wealth fund, and holds senior positions within the Abu Dhabi government -- made such strenuous efforts to hire Guardiola in the first place.
